Hi Emma — great questions. I put together a short options summary and a revised proposal (attached) that maps features to plans and lays out upgrade/downgrade mechanics. High level: 

1) Upgrade path (Business -> Dedicated/Private)
- Migration: mostly config and tenancy mapping. Application traffic is redirected to dedicated endpoints; customer data remains isolated per your preference. Expect ~2-4 days of coordinated cutover for non-critical workloads, up to 10 days for live multi-region rollouts.
- Pricing: you can keep your existing model version pins; billing switches to reserved capacity rates (monthly commit). We include a one-time migration credit equal to one week of hosted spend for upgrades within the first 3 months.

2) Downgrade / credits
- Standard: downgrades are allowed on calendar-month boundaries with 30-day notice. Reserved capacity commits are contractually required for the commit term. If you downgrade early, unused committed spend converts to account credit (not cash) prorated over the remaining months and usable against hosted or add-on spend.

3) Embeddings bundling
- We offer a flat monthly embedding bundle (X million vectors) as an add-on on Business and Dedicated. Overages billed per-embedding-call rate. Bundles are discounted vs call-by-call at scale.

4) Feature mapping (summary in attached PDF)
- Business: API access (hosted), basic RBAC, standard logs (90-day retention), streaming, function calling.
- Enterprise: Dedicated/Private, advanced RBAC + SCIM, KMS/HSM support, audit logs (1y+), SLA-backed latency/uptime, and longer retention options.

I attached proposal_v2.pdf with three price bands and a recommended path for a 6- vs 12-month commit. Bullet items on page 3 show the concessions we can make for shorter commits.

If it helps, Marissa (cc’d) can add notes on the observability and rollout checklist.

Best,
Dylan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Emma — quick technical clarifications to supplement Dylan’s note: 

- Migration/Upgrade: No code changes should be required for most customers. The main work is endpoint and secret rotation across environments. We maintain model hashes/versions so inference results are reproducible post-migration.
- Embedding bundles: Bundles are pooled at the org level; you can assign sub-accounts for spend reporting. If you plan to run heavy reranking or semantic search, the bundle plus our prefix caching reduces calls by ~35–50% depending on query overlap.
- SLA & security: For the Enterprise tier we support KMS integrations (AWS/GCP/Azure), customer-managed keys for Private, and SOC2 + yearly pen test evidence.

I also attached a draft SOW showing a realistic rollout timeline and responsibilities — feedback welcome.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) Discount: proposal_v2 shows 15% off for 12-months. Procurement wants the same effective price but with a 6-month commit. Is there flexibility to split the difference (e.g., 12% for 6 months + sign a 9-month extension on mutual termination)?
2) Credits: if we do a 6-month commit and then grow into Dedicated, can unused money be converted to reserved capacity rather than account credits?
3) Feature clarity: can you provide a one-page table that explicitly lists which RBAC/observability items are in Business vs Enterprise (our legal needs that for contract review).
4) SLA: We also need clarity on uptime and remedy for downtime (credits vs service-level escalation).

If you can send a redlineable proposal (one page) and the feature table by tomorrow, we can move to legal review quickly.

Thanks,

Liam — appreciate the clear asks. Short answers and next steps: 

1) Discount/term flexibility: We can offer 12% off list for a 6-month initial commit, with an automatic option to extend to 9 months at the same rates (mutual opt-out with 30 days). That gets you most of the commercial benefit without a full 12-month lock-in.

2) Credit conversion: If you upgrade into Dedicated within 90 days of conversion, unused committed spend can be applied directly to reserved capacity invoices (not just account credit). After 90 days unused funds fall back to credit. Will document exact mechanics in the redline.

3) Feature table & SLA: Attached here is a one-page feature matrix (see proposal_v2 page 2). SLA terms: 99.95% uptime for Dedicated/Private with financial credits tied to monthly uptime buckets; hosted Business has a 99.9% target with operational fallbacks. Legal can redline the precise remedy language — we won’t push for indemnities beyond standard enterprise terms.

4) Trial for Optimize: as a gesture for the shorter commit, we’ll include a 3-month complimentary trial of Redwood Optimize for your primary workload (caching + batching tuning) to reduce unit cost early.

Next steps: I’ll upload a redlineable one-pager to DocuSign and a cleaned feature table to the HubSpot record. If that all looks good, please have procurement send the redline back and we’ll route to legal.
